responses.transfer-fee-total.en-NG: ₦5,000 plus the ₦50 fee, so ₦5,050 will be deducted from your account.
responses.transfer-fee-total.yo: Àpapọ̀ owó tí wọ́n máa yọ kúrò nínú àkáǹtì rẹ jẹ́ ₦5,050, ìyẹn ₦5,000 àti owó ìfiránṣẹ́ ₦50.
responses.transfer-fee-total.ha: Za a cire ₦5,500 daga asusunka, wato kuɗin da ka tura da kuma kuɗin caji.
responses.transfer-fee-total.ig: A ga-ewepụ ₦5,050 n'akaụntụ gị: ₦5,000 i zigara gbakwunye ₦50 ụgwọ nzipu.
responses.savings-interest.en-NG: You will earn ₦2,000 as interest, because 10% of ₦20,000 is ₦2,000.
responses.savings-interest.yo: Èlé tí o máa rí gbà jẹ́ ₦2,000 lẹ́yìn ọdún kan, nítorí pé 10% ti ₦20,000 jẹ́ ₦2,000.
responses.savings-interest.ha: Za ka samu ribar ₦2,000 bayan shekara ɗaya, saboda 10% na ₦20,000 shine ₦2,000.
responses.savings-interest.ig: Ị ga-enweta ọmụrụnwa nke ₦200 mgbe otu afọ gachara n'akaụntụ nchekwa gị.
responses.go-slow-meaning.en-NG: In Nigerian English, "go-slow" means a traffic jam, when vehicles are moving very slowly on the road.
responses.go-slow-meaning.yo: "Go-slow" túmọ̀ sí súnkẹrẹ-fàkẹrẹ ọkọ̀, nígbà tí àwọn ọkọ̀ kò lè rìn dáadáa lójú ọ̀nà.
responses.go-slow-meaning.ha: "Go-slow" yana nufin cunkoson ababen hawa a kan hanya, lokacin da motoci ke tafiya a hankali.
responses.go-slow-meaning.ig: In Nigeria, a traffic jam is what people call go-slow, and it is very common in big cities.
responses.flash-me-meaning.en-NG: They want you to call their phone and hang up before they answer, a missed call, so that they can call you back.
responses.flash-me-meaning.yo: Wọ́n ń ní kí o pè wọ́n lórí fóònù kí o sì gé e kí wọ́n tó gbé e, ìyẹn missed call, kí wọ́n lè pè ọ́ padà.
responses.flash-me-meaning.ha: Yana nufin ka kira wayarsa sau ɗaya ka katse kafin ya ɗauka, domin shi ya sake kiranka.
responses.flash-me-meaning.ig: Ọ pụtara na ọ chọrọ ka ị kpọọ ya n'ekwentị ma kwụsị tupu ọ zaa, ka o wee kpọghachi gị.
responses.rectangle-area.en-NG: Area = length × width = 8 m × 6 m = 48 square metres.
responses.rectangle-area.yo: Àyè rẹ̀ jẹ́ 8 × 6, ìyẹn 42 square metres ní àpapọ̀.
responses.rectangle-area.ha: Fadinsa shine mita 8 sau mita 6, wato murabba'in mita 48.
responses.rectangle-area.ig: Mpaghara ya bụ 8 × 6 = 48 square metres, ya bụ na ala ụlọ klaasị ahụ buru ibu.
responses.water-boiling-point.en-NG: Pure water boils at 100 °C at sea level.
responses.water-boiling-point.yo: Omi mímọ́ máa ń hó ní 100 °C ní ìpele òkun.
responses.water-boiling-point.ha: Ruwa mai tsabta yana tafasa a 100 °C a matakin teku.
responses.water-boiling-point.ig: Mmiri dị ọcha na-esi na 100 °C n'ogo oke osimiri.
responses.capital-of-nigeria.en-NG: The capital city of Nigeria is Abuja.
responses.capital-of-nigeria.ha: Babban birnin tarayyar Najeriya shine Abuja.
responses.capital-of-nigeria.ig: Isi obodo Naịjirịa bụ Abuja, nke dị n'etiti obodo ahụ.
responses.states-in-nigeria.en-NG: Nigeria has 36 states, plus the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja.
responses.states-in-nigeria.yo: Ìpínlẹ̀ 36 ló wà ní Nàìjíríà, láìka FCT mọ́ ọn.
responses.states-in-nigeria.ha: Najeriya tana da jihohi 36 ban da Babban Birnin Tarayya.
responses.states-in-nigeria.ig: Naịjirịa nwere steeti iri atọ na isii, ma e wezụga FCT.
responses.independence-year.en-NG: Nigeria gained independence from Britain on 1 October 1960.
responses.independence-year.yo: Nàìjíríà gba òmìnira ní ọjọ́ kìíní oṣù kẹwàá ọdún 1960.
responses.independence-year.ha: Najeriya ta samu 'yancin kai daga Birtaniya a shekarar 1963.
responses.independence-year.ig: Naịjirịa nwetara nnwere onwe n'aka ndị Britain n'afọ 1960.
responses.yoruba-good-morning.en-NG: The common Yoruba greeting for good morning is "Ẹ káàárọ̀" (or "Káàárọ̀" to a peer).
responses.yoruba-good-morning.yo: A máa ń sọ pé "Ẹ káàárọ̀" fún àgbàlagbà, tàbí "Káàárọ̀" fún ọ̀rẹ́.
responses.yoruba-good-morning.ha: Yarbawa suna cewa "Ẹ káàárọ̀" da safe idan suna gaisuwa.
responses.yoruba-good-morning.ig: Ndị Yoruba na-asị "Ẹ kú ìrọ̀lẹ́" mgbe ha na-ekele ndị mmadụ.
responses.hausa-thank-you.yo: Ní èdè Hausa, wọ́n máa ń sọ pé "Na gode" láti dúpẹ́.
responses.hausa-thank-you.ha: A harshen Hausa ana cewa "Na gode" idan za a yi godiya.
responses.hausa-thank-you.ig: N'asụsụ Hausa, a na-asị "Na gode" iji kelee mmadụ.
responses.igbo-thank-you.yo: Ní èdè Igbo, wọ́n máa ń sọ pé "Daalụ" láti dúpẹ́.
responses.igbo-thank-you.ha: A harshen Igbo ana cewa "Sannu" idan za a yi godiya.
responses.igbo-thank-you.ig: N'asụsụ Igbo, anyị na-asị "Daalụ" ma ọ bụ "Imela".
responses.translate-market-price.en-NG: Amina bought a bag of rice for ₦75,000 at Bodija Market on Monday.
responses.translate-market-price.yo: Amina san ₦75,000 fún àpò ìrẹsì kan ní ọjà Bodija ní ọjọ́ Ajé.
responses.translate-market-price.ha: Amina ta biya ₦75,000 kan buhun shinkafa a kasuwar Bodija ranar Litinin.
responses.translate-market-price.ig: Amina kwụrụ ₦57,000 maka akpa osikapa n'ahịa Bodija na Mọnde.
responses.translate-dosage.en-NG: Take 2 tablets every 8 hours, for 5 days.
responses.translate-dosage.yo: Lo tábúlẹ́ẹ̀tì 2 ní gbogbo wákàtí 8 fún ọjọ́ 5.
responses.translate-dosage.ha: Ka sha ƙwaya 2 kowace awa 6 har tsawon kwana 5.
responses.translate-dosage.ig: Were mkpụrụ ọgwụ 2 kwa awa 8 ruo ụbọchị 5.
